assumptions: Cases use a fictional northpine.example project (traffic snapshot, organic audit findings, Page decisions), synthetic Search Console rows and a stubbed model answer; tests/test_site_architecture.py supplies them offline. They are not live evidence.
The plan reads no repository. Possible orphans come from the audit's crawl sample (at most 100 pages); click depth is not measured.
cost_drivers: Up to three Search Console reads and one gpt-6-luna call of up to 20,000 input bytes and 2,048 output tokens; a stop report makes no model call. Unmeasured until qualification.
effects: Replaces reports/organic/site-architecture/SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md. The technical fix later asks about each row in its redirects.json block; nothing here edits a page, redirect or PR.

cases.description: /features moves to /product, and an old /old-reports redirect points at a page that moves too. The plan retargets /old-reports straight at /product/reports and asks about /features/invoicing, which has clicks and no new route.
No planned change; the audit's crawl sample flags /pricing as a possible orphan. The gate passes on that, labelled as the crawl sample, and click depth is said to be not measured.
One page in Search Console, no audit, snapshot or Page decisions and no trigger: a clean stop with explicit unknowns.
No applied_on input: the follow-up stops and asks for the date before any comparison.
The 12-month page read comes back truncated during a URL change; the plan states incomplete coverage instead of false zeros.

rubric.question: Does every number name its source and window (Search Console 12 months, snapshot 28 days, the audit's crawl sample), with click depth said to be not measured rather than guessed?
Is every moved must-keep URL represented once, with no chain, no source that is also a target and no unrelated home redirect, and does the redirects.json block match the table?
Does the gate pass or stop only on supported evidence, with unknown kept apart from zero?
